description: High level overview dashboard for Tetragon Enterprise (part of Isovalent Platform). At a glance, should provide strong indicators of potential issues in the cluster. Indicators here are designed to provide opinionated thresholds on problematic Tetragon metrics.

options.content:
ℹ️ High level health indicators on Tetragon components in a Kubernetes cluster, such as whether components are in a running state (i.e. not Pending/Crashing etc).

Note: this section requires metrics exported by [kube-state-metrics](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/kube-state-metrics/).

targets.expr: sum by (version, time) (tetragon_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.description: Tracks the running state of Tetragon Pods such as the Agent and the Operator. A non-zero number of not running Tetragon Pods could indicate the number of Pods that are crashing, cannot be scheduled (i.e. Pending), or having image pull issues, etc.

targets.expr: count(kube_pod_status_phase{pod=~"tetragon-[0-9a-z]+", container="tetragon", phase!="Running", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} == 1 or kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{pod=~"tetragon-[0-9a-z]+", container="tetragon", reason=~"CrashLoopBackOff|ErrImagePull|ImagePullBackOff|Init:CrashLoopBackOff", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} > 0) or vector(0)
count(kube_pod_container_status_running{pod=~"tetragon-[0-9a-z]+", container="tetragon", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} > 0)

count(kube_pod_status_phase{pod=~"tetragon-operator-.+", phase!="Running", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} == 1 or kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{pod=~"tetragon-operator-.+", reason=~"CrashLoopBackOff|ErrImagePull|ImagePullBackOff|Init:CrashLoopBackOff", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} > 0) or vector(0)
count(kube_pod_container_status_running{pod=~"tetragon-operator-.+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} > 0)

options.content:
ℹ️ Tetragon uses BPF maps as a datastore.

**These maps are fundamental to Tetragon's operations. If they reach capacity then related functionality may fail.**

panels.description:
Utilization of BPF maps, which act as data stores for Tetragon.  

High values can indicate overutilization of BPF maps and may lead to degradation of functionality. This graph calculates total utilization across all Tetragon nodes and it might not highlight outlier nodes with higher pressure.

targets.expr: sum(tetragon_map_entries{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", map!~"tg_socket_tuple_map"}) by (map) / sum(tetragon_map_capacity{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}) by (map) or label_replace(sum(tetragon_inode_map_entries{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}) / sum(tetragon_inode_map_max{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}), "map", "hash_map_inode_alloc", "", "")

panels.title: Total Map Utilization

panels.description:
Utilization of BPF maps, which act as data stores for Tetragon.  

High values can indicate overutilization of BPF maps and may lead to degradation of functionality. This graph shows top k maps with the highest utilization across all Tetragon nodes. If you spot an outlier pod, you can select it in a dashboard filter for more insights.

Legend format:
<map> : <policy (if applicable)> : <Tetragon pod>

targets.expr: topk($k, tetragon_map_entries{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", map!~"tg_socket_tuple_map"} / tetragon_map_capacity{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} or label_replace(tetragon_inode_map_entries{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"} / tetragon_inode_map_max{pod=~"$pod", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}, "map", "hash_map_inode_alloc", "", ""))

panels.title: Map Utilization (current, top k)

options.content:
ℹ️ Memory and CPU consumption of Tetragon components.

For more information about understanding Tetragon memory consumption, refer to [Tetragon Troubleshooting Documentation](https://docs.isovalent.com/operations-guide/tetragon/troubleshooting/index.html#understanding-tetragon-memory-consumption).

Note: some panels in this section require metrics exported by [cAdvisor](https://github.com/google/cadvisor) (in Kubernetes they're provided by kubelet) and [kube-state-metrics](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics).

panels.description: Memory consumption of Tetragon agents

targets.expr: topk($k, sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", container="", }) by (pod))

panels.title: Tetragon Agent Container Memory Consumption (current, top k)

panels.description: CPU consumption of Tetragon agents

targets.expr: topk($k, sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", container="", cpu="total"}[$__rate_interval])) by (pod))

panels.title: Tetragon Agent Container CPU Consumption (current, top k)

panels.description: Memory consumption of Tetragon agents

targets.expr: topk($k, sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[0-9a-z]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", container=""}) by (pod))

panels.title: Tetragon Agent Container Memory Consumption (top k)

panels.description: CPU consumption of Tetragon agents

targets.expr: topk($k, sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", container="", cpu="total"}[$__rate_interval])) by (pod))

panels.title: Tetragon Agent Container CPU Consumption (top k)

panels.description:
This graph shows how close Tetragon Agent Pods are to their memory requests. By default Tetragon installs without explicit memory request - in which case nothing should be shown here. However, if Tetragon has a memory request set, this graph shows how much of their requests pods are using.

For more details about resource management in Kubernetes see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/.

Note: this panel requires metrics exported by [kube-state-metrics](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/kube-state-metrics/).

targets.expr: (sum by (pod, container)(container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"})) / (sum by (pod, container) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", resource="memory"}))

panels.title: Tetragon Agent Container Memory Request Utilization

panels.description:
This metric provides the 50th (i.e. median) percentile of Tetragon agent runtime scheduling.

This is related to CPU availability and utilization, high values or increases here denote in either throttling or lack of compute resources.

High sustained runtime will likely indicate problems with Tetragon functionality.

targets.expr: topk($k, histogram_quantile(0.50, sum(rate(go_sched_latencies_seconds_bucket{pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le, pod)) )

panels.title: Tetragon Agent CPU Runtime Latency (P50) (current, top k)

panels.description:
This metric provides the 95th percentile of Tetragon agent runtime scheduling.

This is related to CPU availability and utilization, high values or increases here denote in either throttling or lack of compute resources.

High sustained runtime will likely indicate problems with Tetragon functionality.

targets.expr: topk($k, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(go_sched_latencies_seconds_bucket{pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le, pod)) )

panels.title: Tetragon Agent CPU Runtime Latency (P95) (current, top k)

panels.description:
This graph shows how close Tetragon Agent Pods are to their memory limits. By default Tetragon installs without explicit memory limit - in which case nothing should be shown here. However, if Tetragon has a memory limit set, this graph shows how much of their limits pods are using.

Pods that hit their limit will be killed for running out of memory by the Linux host OS and can cause disruptions in functionality. Consistently high values here should indicate that you may want to increase limits.

For more details about resource management in Kubernetes see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/.

Note: this panel requires metrics exported by [kube-state-metrics](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/kube-state-metrics/).

targets.expr: (sum by (pod, container)(container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"})) / (sum by (pod, container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{pod=~"$pod", pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", resource="memory"}))

panels.title: Tetragon Agent Container Memory Limit Utilization

panels.description:
This metric provides the 95th and 50th (i.e. median) percentile of Tetragon agent runtime scheduling.

This is related to CPU availability and utilization, high values or increases here denote in either throttling or lack of compute resources.

High sustained runtime will likely indicate problems with Tetragon functionality.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(go_sched_latencies_seconds_bucket{pod=~"tetragon-[a-z0-9]+", namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le))
